records.title: Signing authority is now one enforced check on every signing route and approver/reviewer can be assigned; residuals: SCIM cannot assign signing roles, lock commands have no role gate, admins sign by default
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: server/services/part11/signing-authority-gate.ts:44-55 checkSigningAuthority (membership-row role via resolve-signer-role.ts:25-44, fail-closed 503 on lookup error) is now the only authority check. /api/c2c/actions/sign and /revoke-signature ask it before re-auth regardless of GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE (server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:113 SIGNATURE_COMMANDS, :667-670 before verifyReauth :673). AnA e-signature tier asks it before reverifySigner (server/routes/ana-ri/governed-esignature.ts:92 then :98). ESG transmit asks it before re-auth (server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts:300 then :303; technical-rejection :546) and executeGovernedTransmit re-asserts it (server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts:486 -> governed-transmit-checks.ts:218-232). Authoring freeze/e-sign/sign call it (authoring.router.ts:5037, 5311, 7397). Signing roles are assignable: shared/constants/org-roles.ts:32 ASSIGNABLE_ORG_ROLES = admin, approver, manager, reviewer, member, viewer, used by server/routes/tenant-users.ts:34,48 and the Admin UI (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx:86); self re-role refused (tenant-users.ts:595 SELF_ROLE_CHANGE). CI: `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs` -> 'every signer re-verification asks signing authority in its handler; 5 baselined re-authentication(s) sign nothing'; `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.selftest.mjs` -> 27 passed incl. 'the pre-fix Gateway transmit (re-authentication, no authority) fails the authority rule'. `npx vitest run server/routes/c2c/__tests__/governed-sign-authority.test.ts` -> 8/8 (viewer, member, manager refused 403 before password read, nothing written). STILL OPEN: (a) server/routes/scim.ts:70 VALID_ROLES = ['admin','manager','member','viewer'] - an IdP cannot provision approver/reviewer; (b) lock is not in SIGNATURE_COMMANDS (actions.ts:113) and POST /api/c2c/actions/lock (mounted with authMiddleware only, server/bootstrap/register-inline-routes.ts:347) and POST /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock (server/routes/c2c/documents.ts:942-963, mount :819) re-authenticate but apply no role check, so a viewer with their password can lock; (c) DEFAULT_SIGNING_ROLES still includes 'admin' (server/services/part11/signing-authority.ts:23), override only deployment-wide via ESIGNATURE_SIGNING_ROLES - account administration and signing are not segregated; (d) the per-resource permission gate is still dark behind GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE, set nowhere (actions.ts:705-721, governed-signature-ceremony.ts:190).
records.fixedBy: ddc8c0db5 (approver/reviewer assignable, P-18; shared/constants/org-roles.ts:32, tenant-users.ts:34,48); cf950eeb9 (QMS/action sign route authority); b86baf55e (authority on every signing route); 0f961354c (one checkSigningAuthority, ci:sign-ceremony authority rule; signing-authority-gate.ts:44-55, actions.ts:667-670); 505f71263 (authenticator required to sign outside dev/test)
records.remaining: SCIM group mapping cannot assign approver/reviewer (scim.ts:70); /api/c2c/actions/lock and /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock admit any authenticated member including viewer (re-auth and not-author check only); admins hold signing authority by default with no per-org way to segregate it (founder decision); GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE per-resource gate is dead code in practice.
records.severityRationale: The P0 impact is closed: no viewer/member/manager can sign on any signing route, the check runs before the password, and a sponsor can map approvers/reviewers through Admin and access. What remains is not reachable from the UI (no client calls either lock route), affects only SCIM-provisioned orgs (a sales-led pilot can assign roles manually), or is a segregation-of-duties policy choice a small biotech commonly accepts if documented. All are enterprise-GA items.
records.humanTestingNote: Not a defect testers will hit, but a setup prerequisite: only admin, approver or reviewer can sign, and outside NODE_ENV=development/test the signer must have an authenticator enrolled. A manager or member who tries to Approve/Sign/Transmit gets 403 'Your role does not permit applying an electronic signature ... Nothing was signed.' Workaround: in Admin and access assign the tester the Approver or Reviewer role (and enrol an authenticator in Account) before running signing journeys; use a second account for approval because authors cannot approve their own record.
records.instructions:
1. SCIM (engineering): in server/routes/scim.ts replace the local `VALID_ROLES` (line 70) with `ASSIGNABLE_ORG_ROLES` imported from shared/constants/org-roles.ts, so GET /scim/v2/Groups (line ~1147, `let roles = [...VALID_ROLES]`), GET /Groups/:id (~1180) and PATCH /Groups/:id (~1192) accept 'approver' and 'reviewer'. Keep the remove semantics at ~1214 (demote to 'member' only from the group's own role) and the chained audit row via changeMemberRole. Add a test in server/routes/__tests__ (or next to existing scim tests) that is red at HEAD: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/approver add member -> organization_users.role = 'approver' and one chained audit_logs row; GET /Groups lists six groups.
2. Lock role gate (engineering): in server/routes/c2c/actions.ts makeHandler (lines 642-680), for command 'lock' and 'unlock' call `checkSigningAuthority(userId, orgId)` (lock of an artifact is signed with meaning 'release' elsewhere, ARTIFACT_ACT_MEANING in server/services/artifact-approval-act.ts) BEFORE `verifyReauth` and return its status/code exactly as for SIGNATURE_COMMANDS. Do the same in server/routes/c2c/documents.ts POST '/:id/lock' (line 942) before `verifyReauth` (line 959). If the founder prefers editor-level lock, use `editorRoleDecision` from server/services/part11/editor-role.ts instead; either way fail closed (503) when the role lookup throws. Update the `authority` entries for server/routes/c2c/documents.ts in scripts/ci/sign-ceremony-baseline.json (shrink to 0) and run `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs --write-baseline` only if the gate asks for it.
3. Write tests first (red at HEAD): extend server/routes/c2c/__tests__/governed-sign-authority.test.ts with 'refuses a viewer lock with 403 before the password is read, writing nothing' for /lock and a documents.ts lock test asserting no `UPDATE c2c_documents` and no `password_hash` query for a viewer.
4. Segregation of duties (founder decision first): record whether org admins may sign. If not, remove 'admin' from DEFAULT_SIGNING_ROLES (server/services/part11/signing-authority.ts:23); update server/services/part11/__tests__/one-signing-authority-policy.test.ts, governed-sign-authority.test.ts, the copy at client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx:91 and the `canSign` projection at server/routes/tenant-users.ts:373; and add an Admin and access warning when an organisation has no approver/reviewer (otherwise nobody can sign). If per-org policy is wanted, add an org setting read by `signingAuthorityRoles()` instead of the env var, with its change audited in-transaction.
5. GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE: either enable it in terraform/stack/main.tf boot_environment after validating permission atoms against real role data, or delete the two dark branches (server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:705-721 and server/services/part11/governed-signature-ceremony.ts:190) with their tests so checkSigningAuthority is the single authority path (CLAUDE.md zero duplication). Not a user-facing capability, so no replacement path is needed, but name checkSigningAuthority in the commit.
6. Work on concept2cure-v2 only; merge, never rebase; run `npm run ci:sign-ceremony` and its selftest before push.
records.acceptance: a) New lock tests fail at HEAD (viewer reaches the credential check / lock succeeds) and pass after: viewer and member get 403 ESIGNATURE_NO_AUTHORITY (or the editor refusal) on POST /api/c2c/actions/lock and POST /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock, with no password_hash query and no INSERT/UPDATE. b) SCIM test fails at HEAD (404 'Group not found.' for /Groups/approver) and passes after: approver/reviewer groups listed and assignable, each change with exactly one chained audit_logs row. c) `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs` OK and `check-sign-ceremony.selftest.mjs` all pass. d) Founder decision on admin signing recorded; if admins are removed, an admin's POST /api/c2c/actions/sign returns 403 and an approver's reaches the credential check.
records.dependencies: Founder decision on whether org admins hold signing authority (and whether lock needs signing authority or editor role). None of the engineering steps depends on other findings.

records.title: Unsigned approve-artifact / lock-artifact routes removed; approval and lock exist only as signed acts

The 'do not sign yet' note in server/services/artifact-approval-act.ts:32 is followed by the 2026-10-01 removal note (:34-36); the remedy sentences (:183-200) now name only the signed status route / AnA signed act. promote_artifact no longer sets 'approved' (server/services/ai-actions/handlers/promote-artifact.ts:14-20, 271-276). Launch-catalog sign writes still baselined in scripts/ci/sign-ceremony-baseline.json (governed-transmit.ts, estar-submission-service.ts, ana-ri/governed-command-signature.ts) are proofs across a function boundary, each with a written reason: the callers re-verify and ask authority first (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:300-303; governed-esignature.ts:92-98; governed-transmit.ts:486) and the writers persist the electronic_signatures row; `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs` -> '20 baselined site(s) remain, exactly as baselined' (24 at the audit).
records.fixedBy: 7038fec50 (D5: the unsigned authoring-actions approve and lock routes are removed; server/routes/authoring-actions.ts:820-835); signed replacements hardened by 0f961354c (checkSigningAuthority on the status route and AnA signed act)
records.severityRationale: No unsigned approval or lock path remains for concept2cure artifacts; both doors that set approved/locked are electronic signatures with re-auth, authority and a signature row in the same transaction, and the removed routes answer 404 with nothing written (pinned by test). The ordering of the transmit signature relative to the send is tracked separately as P11-07.

records.title: QMS controlled documents: draft-to-effective and unsigned-effective holes closed, but the signature still covers no SOP content, versions are overwritten on revise, retirement is signed 'APPROVED', and the register shows no signature
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED: approval only from 'in_review' (server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts:120 APPROVABLE_STATES = ['in_review']; was ['draft','in_review'] at 92ccdba1:112) and the register offers 'Send for review' first (client/src/concept2cure/quality/SopRegister.tsx:415-429). The database now refuses an effective/retired document without a same-transaction signature (migrations/20261001_qms_document_signature_required.sql, in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2975). Change-control writes carry requireEditorAccess (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:1360,1401,1424,1526,1563,1588). Approve/retire check signing authority before the credential (mdx-qms.ts:563-600). The AnA create_qms_document role-check bullet was already wrong at 92ccdba1: it is a 'confirm' tool and the central writeRoleRefusal gate (AnaToolExecutor.ts:547-561 at HEAD; :425,444 at 92ccdba1) applies the editor role. STILL OPEN: (1) computeQmsDocumentContentDigest (document-approval-signature.ts:129-147) hashes the register row, metadata (a section skeleton: key/label/order/hint only, mdx-qms.ts:150-155) and the artifactId POINTER; no SOP body is stored or hashed, qms_documents.artifact_id has no FK (shared/schema.ts:19685) and nothing locks the linked content; the AnA create path does not set artifact_id at all. (2) No version table (grep for qms_document_versions/qms_document_revisions finds nothing); revise overwrites version, approver_id, approved_at in place (HTTP mdx-qms.ts:668-684; AnA revise_qms_document AnaToolExecutor.ts ~14323), so v1's approved content cannot be retrieved. (3) Retirement signs with the approval literal: retireBody = approveBody.omit(...) (mdx-qms.ts:528) whose meaning is z.literal('APPROVED'); retireQmsDocumentSigned stores params.meaning (document-approval-signature.ts:498,545); the client dialog passes meanings={['approval']} (SopRegister.tsx:617). (4) The register row (SopRegister.tsx:377-470) shows number, title, type, version, status, effective and review dates - no approver, signed-at or meaning; only a toast after signing (quality/qmsApproval.ts:40-54). A CSV compliance report with signer/meaning exists (server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/controlled-documents.ts:34-50) but no UI or PDF manifestation. (5) Send for review is an unsigned PATCH; PATCH writes its audit row after commit with field names only (mdx-qms.ts:496-506).
records.fixedBy: cf950eeb9 (approval only from in_review; document-approval-signature.ts:120); 5726976d0 (DB refuses effective/retired without signature; migrations/20261001_qms_document_signature_required.sql); f1d2589ff (change-control writes need an editor); c6f2028b2 (legacy /api/qms deleted, canonical QMS writes refuse a viewer)
records.remaining: Signature content binding (no controlled SOP body is stored or hashed, linked artifact not locked); no append-only version history (revise overwrites in place); retirement meaning is 'APPROVED'; no signature manifestation (name, UTC time, meaning) in the register or a printable record; review step unsigned; PATCH audit after commit with field names only.
records.severityRationale: QMS controlled documents is in the launch catalog. A pilot customer using it for document control would fail a §11.70 / §11.10(e) / 21 CFR 820.40 audit: the approval signature does not bind any procedure text, prior approved versions are not retained, and retirement records a false meaning (§11.50). Not P0 because the database now prevents an unsigned effective document and approval requires review first, so no unsigned or unreviewed SOP can become effective.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers can create, send for review, approve and retire SOPs. Visible defects: the register never shows who approved a document, when, or with what meaning (only a transient toast); the Retire dialog's only meaning is 'approval'; after Revise (via AnA) the previous approver/approval date disappear from the row and the earlier version cannot be opened; there is no place to write or view the SOP body in the register (clicking the number only asks AnA). Workaround for verifying signatures: Reporting -> controlled documents compliance report (CSV) lists the standing approval signature per document.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decision (record it before coding): what is the system of record for SOP body text - (a) a body stored on the QMS version itself, or (b) a linked Authoring document (authoring_documents / concept2cure artifact). Also decide the retirement meaning word and whether 'Send for review' must be a signed 'REVIEWED' act.
2. Schema (Rule 1: new file, additive, IF NOT EXISTS; new table in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL): add migrations/2026MMDD_qms_document_versions.sql creating public.qms_document_versions (id serial PK, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id), document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES qms_documents(id), version TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, body JSONB or TEXT per decision, body_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, linked_artifact_id INTEGER NULL, linked_content_sha256 TEXT NULL, approval_signature_id INTEGER NULL, created_by INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE (document_id, version)), plus a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises (append-only). Insert it in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs) before the final RLS sweep pair; run `npm run ci:migration-set-order` and `npm run ci:migration-drop-safety`. Add the trigger to the expected list in server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts so the boot gate checks it. Mirror the table in shared/schema.ts next to qmsDocuments (line ~19668).
3. Bind content: in server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts approveQmsDocumentSigned, inside the caller's transaction after the FOR UPDATE read, (a) read the controlled body per the decision (for a linked artifact: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and compute its content sha256; refuse with 409 if none), (b) INSERT the qms_document_versions snapshot, (c) add bodySha256/linkedContentSha256 to computeQmsDocumentContentDigest and change QMS_DOCUMENT_BINDING_BASIS to a new value (e.g. 'qms-document-version-content-sha256-v2') so pre-change rows remain verifiable under the old basis, (d) set approval_signature_id on the snapshot after persistGovernedActionSignature returns. For a linked artifact, lock it (status 'locked' through the existing signed-act path or a write-lock check in the authoring FROZEN/APPROVED middleware, authoring.router.ts ~423-470) so post-approval edits are refused; add a verdict helper that recomputes and reports 'does not cover' if the linked content hash differs.
4. Revise: in server/routes/mdx-qms.ts POST /qms/documents/:id/revise (650-712) move to one transaction (pool.connect, BEGIN, setTenantContextTx), assert the outgoing version has a snapshot row, then UPDATE and write the chained audit row with recordGovernedAction(client, ...) (as the AnA twin does at AnaToolExecutor.ts ~14307-14343) instead of the after-commit recordAuditRow at :691. Add GET /qms/documents/:id/versions returning snapshots with their signature.
5. Retirement meaning: add the chosen word to TASK_SIGNATURE_MEANINGS (server/services/part11/signature-meanings.ts:10-15, which flows into GOVERNED_SIGN_MEANINGS) and to client/src/concept2cure/_shared/esignMeanings.ts; export QMS_DOCUMENT_RETIREMENT_MEANING from document-approval-signature.ts; make retireBody (mdx-qms.ts:528) accept only that literal; change SopRegister.tsx:617 meanings to it.
6. Manifestation: extend GET /qms/documents (mdx-qms.ts:340) and GET /qms/documents/:id (:433) with a LEFT JOIN LATERAL to the standing approval/retirement signature (reuse the STANDING predicate from server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/controlled-documents.ts:24-26: signer_name, signed_at, signature_meaning, bound_payload_digest); add 'Approved by', 'Signed (UTC)' and 'Meaning' to the row grid and a detail panel in SopRegister.tsx; if the founder requires a printable record, add a PDF of the version with its signature block.
7. If the founder makes review a signed act: turn the draft->in_review PATCH into POST /qms/documents/:id/review using verifyApprovalSigner with meaning 'REVIEWED' and an electronic_signatures row of type 'qms-document-review'; refuse approval unless a standing review signature exists for the same version digest.
8. Write every test red first at HEAD, then green. Work on concept2cure-v2 only; merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: a) Editing the controlled body (or linked artifact) after approval is refused, or the signature verdict for that document reads 'does not cover' (test red at HEAD because the digest ignores content). b) After approve v1.0 -> revise -> approve v2.0, GET /qms/documents/:id/versions returns v1.0 with its body, body_sha256 and approval signature id (red at HEAD: no endpoint/table). c) UPDATE or DELETE on qms_document_versions raises; the boot immutability check lists the new trigger. d) POST /qms/documents/:id/approve on a draft returns 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE (already green - keep as regression). e) POST /retire with meaning 'APPROVED' returns 400; the stored electronic_signatures row for a retirement carries the retirement meaning. f) The register row and detail show printed name, UTC signed time and meaning for an effective document (component test red at HEAD). g) Revise writes its chained audit row in the same transaction: a forced audit failure leaves version/approver unchanged.
records.dependencies: Founder decisions (SOP body system of record; retirement meaning word; signed review step). P11-01 (signing roles) is satisfied at HEAD. Overlaps P11-04 (QMS create/PATCH/revise after-commit audit).

records.title: Audit writes: users, AI accept and the request trail are now transactional/tenant-tagged, but QMS create/edit/revise and eCTD leaf placement still audit after commit, and old_values is never written
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: membership role change/removal write a chained row with previousRole on the caller's transaction (server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts:11-23,51-66,79-99,142-155, used by tenant-users.ts). AI-draft accept writes the revision and authoring audit row (prior and accepted content) inside the content transaction (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:4288-4320, was after-commit 'non-fatal' at 92ccdba1:3667-3673). The request catch-all records the verified tenant (server/startup/audit-trail.ts:79-84,139) into audit.tamper_proof_log.organization_id (db/migrations/20260813_audit_tamper_proof_log.sql:60-62,178-180, amended in place) and is on in terraform with AUDIT_REQUIRE_ENFORCE=true (terraform/stack/main.tf:250-251) and in docker-compose.yml:186 / docker-compose.beta.yml:188. In-transaction writer call sites rose from 25 to 57 for writeChainedAuditRow (grep, non-test server/*.ts). `node scripts/ci/check-discarded-audit-write.mjs` -> '113 baselined across 50 file(s)' (122/54 at the audit). STILL OPEN: writeChainedAuditRow always binds old_values = null (server/services/auditService.ts:306-329, param 13). recordAuditRow (server/services/audit/audit-write-outcome.ts:147-163) is logAction on its own connection after the caller committed; it reports a lost row but cannot roll back. Launch-catalog sites still on it: QMS create (mdx-qms.ts:387, details without prior state), PATCH incl. Send for review (mdx-qms.ts:502, `changedFields` names only, no before/after), HTTP revise (mdx-qms.ts:691), and eCTD leaf create/update (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:3134 and :3195, after the lockSequenceForLeafWrite transaction; update does carry previousDocument). mdx-qms.ts has 17 recordAuditRow + 12 logAction sites and 0 in-transaction writers. The catch-all itself is still fire-and-forget after the response (audit-trail.ts:118-153).
records.fixedBy: 8167aef12 and 0adb1b3ec (role changes, removals and settings changes audited in their transaction; membership-change.ts); 7863cf830 (AI-suggestion/AI-draft accept records in-transaction; authoring.router.ts:4288-4320); 8dab6c8f3 (tamper_proof_log names its tenant; audit-trail.ts:79-84); a8ddcf283 (Compose stacks enable AUDIT_TRAIL_ENABLED)
records.remaining: QMS document create/PATCH/revise (HTTP) and submission leaf create/update audit after commit (loss reported, not prevented); QMS PATCH records field names only; audit_logs.old_values is never populated by any writer; discarded-audit baseline still 113 sites (launch files: authoring.router.ts 1, section-generation-service.ts 1, estar-submission-service.ts 2).
records.severityRationale: The pilot's most-used governed paths (authoring saves and AI accept, Vault ingest/metadata, membership changes, every signature/approval/retire) now commit their audit row with the change, and every mutating request is additionally recorded with tenant and actor by a trail production refuses to boot without. The residual after-commit sites report a lost row to the user rather than hiding it, and leaf re-pointing records the previous document. Missing before-values on QMS draft edits and an always-null old_values column remain a customer-QA finding to close before enterprise GA; the QMS-specific record integrity is tracked at P1 under P11-03.
records.humanTestingNote: Not observable in normal testing. Only if the audit store fails after a QMS create/edit or leaf placement does the response carry meta.auditTrail.persisted=false (surfaced to the user as 'saved, but its audit record was not written'); the change itself stays.
records.instructions:
1. old_values: extend AuditLogEntry (server/services/auditService.ts) with an optional `oldValues` object and bind it to parameter 13 in writeChainedAuditRow (line ~322, currently `null`), JSON-stringified like new_values. Keep the payload hash over new_values unchanged so existing chains verify; if oldValues should be tamper-evident, add it to the hashed payload only for rows written after a dated cut-over and document that in the function header.
2. QMS create (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:361-399): replace the autocommitted pool.query + recordAuditRow with one transaction (const client = await pool.connect(); BEGIN; setTenantContextTx(client, orgId)), INSERT ... RETURNING *, then `await writeChainedAuditRow(client, { tenantId: orgId, userId, action: 'mdx.qms.document.create', resourceType: 'qms_document', resourceId: String(row.id), details: <created row fields> })`, COMMIT; ROLLBACK on any throw and answer 500 with nothing created. Return meta.auditTrail {persisted:true, chained:true}.
3. QMS PATCH (mdx-qms.ts:448-507): in one transaction SELECT the row FOR UPDATE (same org, status draft/in_review), run the UPDATE, and write the chained row with oldValues = the prior values of exactly the changed columns and details/newValues = the new values (not just names). Same treatment for HTTP revise (650-712): before/after version, approver_id, approved_at in the same transaction (mirror AnaToolExecutor.ts revise_qms_document ~14307-14343).
4. eCTD leaf placement (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts ~3100-3200): move the LEAF_UPDATED and LEAF_CREATED audit writes inside the lockSequenceForLeafWrite callback, on its transaction (use the drizzle tx through the repo's queryable adapter, e.g. queryableFromDrizzle, with writeChainedAuditRow), with oldValues = previousDocument; a throw rolls back the placement.
5. Gate: extend scripts/ci/check-discarded-audit-write.mjs (or add ci:after-commit-audit) to refuse `recordAuditRow(` in server/routes/mdx-qms.ts document handlers and server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts leaf functions, with a baseline that can only shrink and a selftest that fails on a reintroduced site. Then run `node scripts/ci/check-discarded-audit-write.mjs --write-baseline` to shrink the 5 files already below their counts.
6. Tests red first (PGlite integration where the suites already use it): force the audit INSERT to fail (e.g. a mocked writeChainedAuditRow throw or a trigger in the test DB) and assert at HEAD the qms_documents/submission_leaves change persists (red), after the fix nothing is written (green).
